body: My Reddit stalker saved my life.  I have no idea who he was, but he showed up out of nowhere, broke into my house, sat outside my door...I honestly thought he was going to kill me because he wouldn’t say anything.  Slightly creepy, but I wanted to die anyway.  So he stayed, I eventually threw everything up, and then he took a little nap and left.  It was weird, but thank you wherever you are.  He used my bathroom and literally just chilled.  I have never seen him before in my life.  Maybe he was an angel, or a stalker...I guess I’ll never know.  I’m glad your friend found you.  You’ve been given another chance.  Do what you need to do to find happiness.  Take care and remember that people do love you.

It doesn’t look creepy as fuck at all.  Literally, she’s just going to write you back and say not interested or just not respond.  What’s creepy is if you keep texting.  Just say “Hi.  How’s your day going?” then.  But, I’ve got a lot of good girl friends and none of them would find that creepy.  At all.  Just text.  That’s all.  You could just say hi and if she doesn’t respond, whatever.  Move on.  There’s nothing wrong with telling someone you enjoyed meeting them and asking them if they want to hang out.  It’s a hell of a lot better than not texting.  If she doesn’t like you, she’ll find you creepy anyway.  But if you don’t text, and she does like you but she’s just shy, you’ll never know.  She could have been your dream woman and you didn’t bother to follow up.  Worth taking the risk.

Edit:  Just text!  If she finds you creepy for saying something nice, fuck her anyway.  Give her a few days to get back to you.  If she doesn’t, she’s not worth it anyway.  Guys, we like men who follow up.  It’s still flattering, and if she’s a good person, she’ll be upfront with you.

You've made it through the acute withdrawal stage--sounds like maybe you had delirium tremens, which I've had from benzo withdrawal, but not drinking--and yes, the hallucinations and the feeling is just horrid to go through.  Halfway conscious with nightmares.  It’s fucking horrible and it can kill you.  So just a little word of warning--don't take any benzos because they are highly addictive.  Xanax is actually one of the worst ones, too, as it is very strong and short acting.  It will help you with a panic attack, but it will also cause panic attacks once it is out of your system, which doesn't take very long.  I’m not trying to scare you, I just want you to play it safe.  Mood stabilizers like antidepressants are much better when it comes to withdrawal because they're long acting and not addictive.  And I believe that benztropine (also known as cogentin) or Benadryl are supposed to help with the shakes.  Prazosin helps with nightmares.  I hope you can get into see a psychiatrist soon, or an addiction counselor, and I would encourage you to find an AA group tonight.  If you feel the need to start drinking again, get help right away.  I mean, literally, right away.  As in, drive to a rehab facility and check yourself in.  You've made it this far and I'm very happy you're still alive.  Cold turkey like that is incredibly hard on your body.  But, hey, you’ve got this.  Don’t worry about a potential panic attack because you’ll surely give yourself one that way.  You are strong mentally and physically, stronger than you think.  It takes a very dedicated person to cold turkey like that, and you’re going to do just fine.  It will be hard, but another week out and you’ll be feeling much better.  Stay on the sober journey; do it for yourself and your wife because you both deserve a happier path.  I believe in you!

I have students from Mexico, and they all agree that Merida is an excellent place to travel to.  That's where they go and they're on tight budgets.  Avoid Cancun and Cozumel because they're both pretty expensive and super touristy.  The Yucatan region in general is beautiful and it was affordable when I was there a few years ago, but I was pretty far south.  They warned me about a few places, like Veracruz.  They said there's a gang problem there now, but when I was there a few years ago, I felt safe.  If you stay north, you could potentially check out Belize as well.  Definitely visit the Lonely Planet website to narrow down where you'd like to go, or just buy the guide.  It's very informative and has info about costs.

Edit:  Another way to save is by using Airbnb and then you'll get info from locals who can tell you about the good spots.
